title: My Plan for Hard Moments
intro: Sometimes feelings get so strong that it is hard to think. You may feel an urge to do something that could make things worse, like yelling, quitting, or shutting everyone out. This plan helps you get through those moments without making them worse. These skills do not fix the problem. They help you ride out the wave until you can think more clearly. Fill out this plan when you are calm. It takes about 15 minutes.

sections.heading: Know your signs
sections.body: What tells you a hard moment is building? Write a few signs on the lines below.
steps: In my thoughts, I notice: ________________________

sections.heading: First: Press pause
steps: Do not act on the urge yet. Tell yourself, 'Not right now. I can wait 10 minutes.'
If you can, move away from the situation. Leave the room, or put down what is in your hands.
Take one slow breath in and a longer breath out.

sections.heading: Next: Calm your body
sections.body: Strong feelings live in the body. When your body calms down, your mind can catch up.
steps: Cool down. Splash cool water on your face, or hold something cold, like a cold drink or an ice pack wrapped in a cloth, for a short time.
Slow your breathing. Make each breath out a bit longer than the breath in.
Burn off energy, if your body allows. Walk fast, climb stairs, or do jumping jacks for a few minutes.
Tense and let go. Squeeze your hands or lift your shoulders for 5 seconds. Then let them relax.

sections.heading: Then: Get through the next few minutes
sections.body: Pick things that fill your mind or bring you comfort. Choose ones that are safe and free or low-cost.
steps: Do something that takes your full attention, like a puzzle, a game, cooking, or cleaning.
Give your mind a job, like counting back from 100 by 7s or naming every blue thing in the room.
Call or text someone and talk about something else. Or help someone with a small task.
Find a comfort, like a warm shower, a soft blanket, calm music, a smell you like, or a cup of tea sipped slowly.

sections.heading: Remind yourself why waiting helps
sections.body: Do this part now, while you are calm. Then read it when a hard moment comes.
steps: When I act on the urge, what usually happens later? ________________
When I wait it out, what usually happens later? ________________
A short note to myself for a hard moment: ________________

sections.heading: Reach out
steps: A person I can call or text: ________________________
A place I can go to be around others: ________________________
My counselor or therapist: ________________________

sections.heading: Tips
steps: Practice these skills when you are a little upset, not just in a crisis. Then they will come more easily when you need them.

Cold water and hard exercise change your heart rate. Ask your doctor first if you have a heart problem, an eating problem, or other health concerns, or if you are pregnant. Until then, use gentler options.
These skills are for short-term relief. If you find yourself using them to avoid all hard feelings, talk with your counselor.
Keep this plan where you can find it fast, like in your bag or by your bed.
If you have thoughts of suicide or of hurting yourself, use your safety plan and reach out for help right away.

safetyNote: Safety first: This plan helps with strong feelings and urges. It is not enough on its own if you are thinking about suicide or might hurt yourself or someone else. If that happens, use your safety plan and get help now. In the US, call or text 988 or call 911. In other countries, call your local emergency number or visit findahelpline.com. If someone is hurting you, get to a safe place first. Resource only. This sheet does not replace care from a licensed professional.
